question.text: A parallel plate capacitor having a separation between the plates $\mathrm{d}$, plate area $\mathrm{A}$ and material with dielectric constant $\mathrm{K}$ has capacitance $\mathrm{C}_0$. Now one-third of the material is replaced by another material with dielectric constant $2 \mathrm{~K}$, so that effectively there are two capacitors one with area $\frac{1}{3} \mathrm{~A}$, dielectric constant $2 \mathrm{~K}$ and another with area $\frac{2}{3} \mathrm{~A}$ and dielectric constant $\mathrm{K}$.
